sources.README.md:
# Transfer retry panel with decoded progress

This workspace selects files, starts transfers, records queue and progress
history, and paints progress for the open panel. Run it with Node v16.20.2; it
has no dependencies. `src/workspace.js` exports the workspace and the source
helpers used by the host application.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file again does open another visit.
The feed object is shared by attempts and visits for that file. Its `start()`
method may synchronously emit cached data, and `decode(packet)` may return a
value or a Promise.

`recordProgress` appends transfer history. `showProgress` paints the panel.
The queue adapter in `src/queue.js` shows how those two outputs currently relate
to a visit. Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup
retain their existing behavior. Queue records remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}` unless a separate authorization adds
`byteCount` from `file.size`.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: `start()` may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A `showProgress` callback may select or hide
another visit before `start()` returns, while its caller has not yet received
the returned cleanup handle.

The same feed API also has a diagnostic consumer in `src/telemetry.js`.
It is not the panel and must keep its existing behavior while the panel defect
is repaired. `src/progress-source.js` is the host-visible feed implementation;
the navigation and transfer modules show how ownership is handed off when a
listener is released. Host callbacks are synchronous unless their code returns
a Promise.

# Public syntax/build checks
The external public evaluator parses Python/JavaScript/Vue/TypeScript source or checks Go/PHP/Ruby syntax / compiles public Java sources. These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior. Preserve original TASK and public README/source obligations. Independent training Oracle also applies; do not access its implementation or references. No hidden schedules or assertions are included.

public_inputs.task:
A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later
packet arrives. Restore the initial progress update without changing the public
transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, or queue-record behavior. Full
progress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the
current display backward. Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry,
and subsequent uses.

limitations: The progress-frame structure is unspecified, so age must not be inferred from byte counts or other frame fields.
The sources do not specify decode-Promise rejection handling; this guidance does not add such a policy.
The sources require append-only progress history and stale-display suppression, but do not explicitly define the audit ordering of asynchronously decoded frames.
Attempt 2 passing and attempt 1 failing do not prove that their ordering-check difference caused the acceptance result; the evaluator supplied no behavioral failure details.

rules.body: Apply this pattern when a source is shared across attempts or visits, start() may synchronously publish cached or multiple startup packets, decoding may resume asynchronously, and one decoded effect is persistent history while another effect is current-view painting. README.md states: "The feed object is shared by attempts and visits for that file. Its `start()` method may synchronously emit cached data, and `decode(packet)` may return a value or a Promise."

For the panel observer, attach its listener before calling start(); keep consumers with different bootstrap semantics separate. TASK requires: "Restore the initial progress update" while src/telemetry.js specifies: "// Diagnostics count live deltas only. A cached bootstrap is panel state, not a delta."

Assign a watcher-local monotonically increasing receipt token synchronously when each packet arrives, before invoking decode. After decoding, paint only when the watcher is active and the token is greater than the last token actually painted; then advance the painted token before invoking the painting callback. Comparing only with the newest received token can suppress an otherwise valid newer display while an even newer decode is still pending.

Keep persistent and discardable effects distinct: append each decoded frame through recordProgress, but suppress showProgress when its receipt token is not newer than the last painted token or when the originating watcher is inactive. README.md states: "`recordProgress` appends transfer history. `showProgress` paints the panel."

Invalidate the observer before removing its listener, and make release idempotent. If the synchronous painting callback reports that its visit ceased to be current, release immediately so remaining startup emissions and later decode continuations cannot paint. This covers the README.md window: "A `showProgress` callback may select or hide another visit before `start()` returns, while its caller has not yet received the returned cleanup handle."

Do not key validity only by file or feed identity. Retry creates another physical attempt in the same visit, and selecting the same file creates another visit even though the feed is shared; each watcher therefore needs its own active state and receipt/paint counters.

Preserve telemetry's start-before-listener ordering, queue records shaped as `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}`, cancellation and retry behavior, notices, navigation, cleanup, append-only audit delivery, and later reuse of the shared feed. TASK requires: "Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry, and subsequent uses."

Verify warm cached startup, multiple synchronous startup packets, immediate and out-of-order Promise decoding, live post-start streaming, retry replacement, same-file reselection, hide/disposal during showProgress, in-flight completion after release, idempotent removal, telemetry bootstrap exclusion, and unchanged queue-record shape. Run the public JavaScript syntax/build checks as a separate non-behavioral verification.

checkpoints: Attach the panel progress listener before invoking the panel feed's start(), because start() may synchronously emit cached progress.
Assign ordering at packet receipt, before decode completion, so Promise settlement order cannot redefine frame age.
Before painting a decoded frame, verify that it is the newest received frame eligible for that watcher and that its visit is still current.
Make startup cleanup effective even when showProgress synchronously selects another visit or hides the panel before start() returns.
Run the public JavaScript syntax/build checks after any Action; they do not replace behavioral verification.
forbidden_effects: Do not change the public transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, cancellation, notice, or queue-record behavior.
Do not add byteCount or otherwise change queue records from {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}.
Do not treat the cached bootstrap as a diagnostic telemetry delta or change telemetry's existing start/listener behavior.
Do not suppress ordinary live progress merely because decoding is asynchronous.
Do not let a detached, cancelled, hidden, replaced, or disposed panel watcher paint later decode results or synchronous startup packets.
Do not infer frame ordering from decode completion time or from an unspecified field within a progress frame.
lifecycle_identity: A panel progress watcher belongs to one physical transfer attempt, identified by its attemptId, and to that attempt's originating visit.
Retry keeps the same visit but creates a new physical attempt; progress from the replaced attempt must not become current for the retry attempt.
Selecting the same file again creates a new visit even though the file's feed object is shared; watcher validity must therefore not be keyed only by file or feed identity.
Frame age is scoped to one watcher and determined by that watcher's packet-reception order, not Promise settlement order.
Telemetry is a separate consumer with its own lifecycle and is not the panel watcher.

obligations.text: A warm panel progress source must deliver its initial cached progress during transfer startup, without waiting for a later packet.
If start() synchronously emits multiple packets, the panel watcher must observe them in source emission order and establish their age before decoding.
When full frames decode out of order, completion of an older received frame must not replace a display already produced by a newer received frame.
Progress history must continue to append decoded transfer frames; display stale-suppression must not silently redefine or discard the existing audit stream.
Once the originating watcher is released by cancellation, retry replacement, navigation, hiding, or disposal, it must not paint subsequent progress, including decode continuations already in flight.
Synchronous reentry from showProgress during start() must honor the newly selected, hidden, or disposed state before any remaining startup delivery and must leave the released listener cleaned up.
Ordinary post-start streaming must continue to record progress and paint progress for the current visit.
Diagnostic telemetry must retain its existing behavior: it counts live deltas and does not count the cached bootstrap emitted by start().
Transfer creation, retry acceptance, visit creation, notices, cancellation callbacks, cleanup, and queue-record shape and retention must remain unchanged.
The shared feed must remain usable by later attempts, later visits, and telemetry consumers after an earlier watcher is removed.

ordering_barriers: For the panel consumer, listener registration must happen before the call to feed.start().
Packet receipt and its monotonically increasing watcher-local order token must happen before invoking feed.decode(packet).
A decoded frame may paint only after comparing its receipt order with the newest eligible receipt order for that watcher.
Listener release or watcher invalidation must commit before synchronous host detachment callbacks can reenter selection or navigation.
Cancellation/replacement/hide/dispose is a barrier after which that watcher may not paint, even if a decode Promise settles later.
Telemetry retains its existing barrier in which feed.start() occurs before telemetry listener registration, excluding cached bootstrap from diagnostics.
preservation: Selecting a file creates a visit; retry replaces the physical attempt without creating another visit; selecting the same file again creates another visit.
The feed remains shared by attempts and visits for the same file.
Queue records remain {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind} and remain retained after their originating panel visit ends.
recordProgress remains the transfer-history output, while showProgress remains the current-panel painting output.
The current-visit guard on panel painting remains effective.
Cancellation invokes onCancel with the file, attemptId, and aborted signal, and repeated cancellation remains inert.
Removal commits before the synchronous host onDetach callback, and repeated listener removal remains inert.
Telemetry continues to ignore cached bootstrap and count live deltas.
decode(packet) continues to support both immediate values and Promises.
Host callbacks retain their existing synchronous behavior unless their own code returns a Promise.

Cover warm cached startup, multiple synchronous startup packets, asynchronous decoding, retry/replacement, navigation, hide, disposal, and later reuse of a shared feed.
Preserve the separate telemetry consumer and all unrelated transfer-workspace behavior.

opening another visit. Selecting the same file again does open another visit.
The feed object is shared by attempts and visits for that file. Its `start()`
method may synchronously emit cached data, and `decode(packet)` may return a
value or a Promise.

`recordProgress` appends transfer history. `showProgress` paints the panel.
The queue adapter in `src/queue.js` shows how those two outputs currently relate
to a visit. Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup
retain their existing behavior. Queue records remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}` unless a separate authorization adds
`byteCount` from `file.size`.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: `start()` may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A `showProgress` callback may select or hide
another visit before `start()` returns, while its caller has not yet received
the returned cleanup handle.

The same feed API also has a diagnostic consumer in `src/telemetry.js`.
It is not the panel and must keep its existing behavior while the panel defect
is repaired. `src/progress-source.js` is the host-visible feed implementation;
the navigation and transfer modules show how ownership is handed off when a
listener is released. Host callbacks are synchronous unless their code returns
a Promise.
